meta.title: Inventories: classification, systems and what to include
meta.summary: Inventory classifications for manufacturers and merchandisers, perpetual and periodic systems, goods in transit and on consignment, which costs to include, and the effects of inventory errors.

videos.title: Classifying inventory
videos.take: Manufacturers report raw materials, work in process and finished goods; merchandisers report one inventory

scenes.say: Inventory is Bluestem's largest current asset: $760,000 of aluminum, half-built kayaks and finished boats.

sub: Assets held for sale in the ordinary course,
or being produced or used to produce them
scenes.say: Inventories are assets held for sale in the ordinary course of business, in production for sale, or to be used in producing goods for sale.

scenes.heading: Two kinds of business
scenes.say: A merchandiser, like Bluestem's dealers, buys finished goods to resell and has one inventory account. A manufacturer like Bluestem has three: raw materials, work in process and finished goods.

scenes.heading: Bluestem, December 31
scenes.say: Bluestem reports raw materials of $210,000, work in process of $95,000, and finished goods of $455,000: $760,000 in total, with the breakdown in the notes.

sub: Inventory drives cost of goods sold,
scenes.say: Inventory errors flow straight into cost of goods sold, gross profit, net income and current assets. Getting it right matters more for Bluestem than for almost any other asset.

scenes.q: Half-built kayaks on the factory floor are reported as:
scenes.say: Quick check. Half-built kayaks on the factory floor are reported as what? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Perpetual and periodic systems
videos.take: Perpetual systems update inventory with every transaction; periodic systems compute COGS at period end

scenes.say: Two systems keep track of inventory. Bluestem's factory uses one; its small retail shop used to use the other.

scenes.heading: Perpetual vs periodic
scenes.say: In a perpetual system, purchases go straight to Inventory and every sale records cost of goods sold. In a periodic system, purchases go to a Purchases account, and cost of goods sold is computed only at the end of the period.

scenes.heading: Periodic: computing COGS
scenes.say: Under periodic, cost of goods sold is beginning inventory plus purchases, which gives goods available for sale, less ending inventory from a physical count. For Bluestem: $680,000 plus $2.6 million, less $760,000, gives $2.52 million.

scenes.heading: Perpetual: a sale
scenes.say: Under perpetual, a sale of kayaks for $9,600 that cost $6,000 records both the revenue and the cost of goods sold at once.

sub: Perpetual records still need a physical
scenes.say: Even with perpetual records, companies count inventory at least once a year. Differences reveal theft, damage and errors, recorded as inventory over and short.

scenes.q: Beginning inventory $50,000; purchases $200,000; ending inventory $70,000. COGS?
scenes.say: Quick check. Beginning inventory fifty thousand; purchases two hundred thousand; ending inventory seventy thousand. Cost of goods sold? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Which goods to include
videos.take: Inventory belongs to whoever has control: check shipping terms and consignment arrangements

scenes.say: The count on December 31 says $732,000. But not everything Bluestem owns was in the warehouse, and not everything in the warehouse is Bluestem's.

scenes.heading: Goods in transit
scenes.say: Goods in transit belong to whoever has control. Under FOB shipping point, control passes when the goods leave the seller, so they're the buyer's. Under FOB destination, they stay the seller's until delivered.
On consignment, the owner, the consignor, ships goods to a dealer, the consignee, who sells them for a commission. The goods stay in the consignor's inventory until sold.

scenes.heading: Adjusting the count
scenes.say: Bluestem adds $15,000 of aluminum shipped to it FOB shipping point, and $22,000 of its kayaks sitting at dealers on consignment. It subtracts $9,000 of paddles it holds for a supplier on consignment. Correct inventory: $760,000.

sub: sales with high rates of return
scenes.say: Other special cases include sales with buyback agreements, which may really be financing, and sales with high rates of return. Control, not location, decides.

scenes.q: Goods shipped to Bluestem FOB destination, still in transit at year-end, belong to:
scenes.say: Quick check. Goods shipped to Bluestem FOB destination, still in transit at year-end, belong to whom? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Which costs to include
videos.take: Product costs, including freight-in, go into inventory; selling and administrative costs are period costs

scenes.say: What goes into the cost of a kayak? More than the price on the supplier's invoice.

scenes.heading: Product vs period costs
scenes.say: Product costs attach to inventory: materials, freight-in, direct labor and manufacturing overhead. Period costs, like selling expenses, administration and freight-out, are expensed when incurred.

scenes.heading: Cost of an aluminum shipment
scenes.say: Bluestem buys aluminum for $50,000, pays $1,800 to have it shipped in, and takes a two percent discount for paying early. Inventory cost is $50,800.

scenes.heading: Recording purchase discounts
scenes.say: Under the gross method, purchases are recorded at the invoice price and discounts taken reduce cost. Under the net method, purchases are recorded net of the discount, and any discount missed is recorded as purchase discounts lost, a financing expense. The net method shows management's missed savings.
Abnormal costs, like spoiled materials or idle plant capacity, are expensed as incurred, not added to inventory. And interest is generally not capitalized on routinely produced inventory.

scenes.q: Which cost is added to inventory?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which cost is added to inventory? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Inventory errors
videos.take: An ending inventory error misstates COGS and income this year and reverses next year

scenes.say: Suppose Bluestem's count had missed the $22,000 of kayaks at dealers. What goes wrong?

scenes.heading: 2027: ending inventory understated $22,000
scenes.say: Understated ending inventory means overstated cost of goods sold, so 2027 income and retained earnings are understated by $22,000, before tax.

scenes.heading: 2028: the error reverses
scenes.say: In 2028, beginning inventory is understated, so cost of goods sold is understated and income overstated by the same amount. By the end of 2028, retained earnings is correct. The error counterbalances.
Counterbalancing doesn't make the error harmless. Both years' income, ratios and trends are wrong, and a covenant could be breached in either year.

sub: income unaffected, assets and liabilities understated
scenes.say: If a purchase is both unrecorded and left out of the count, cost of goods sold and income are right, but inventory and accounts payable are both understated.

scenes.q: Ending inventory is overstated by $10,000. Net income before tax is:
scenes.say: Quick check. Ending inventory is overstated by ten thousand dollars. Net income before tax is what? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Inventory and ethics
videos.take: Inventory is a common place for fraud: cutoff, fake counts and channel stuffing

scenes.say: Because inventory errors move income dollar for dollar, inventory is a favorite target for fraud.

scenes.heading: Classic schemes
scenes.say: Classic schemes include inflating the count, recording January sales in December, counting goods already shipped, and channel stuffing: pushing unordered goods onto dealers to book revenue.
Good cutoff means each purchase and sale lands in the right period. Auditors test shipments and receipts around year-end and observe the physical count.
Red flags for analysts: inventory growing much faster than sales, falling turnover, and gross margins that look too good.
Bluestem uses count teams independent of the warehouse staff, numbered count tags, and a cutoff review of the last ten shipping documents each year.

scenes.q: Pushing extra unordered goods onto dealers at year-end to boost sales is called:

case: Bluestem's count team reports $732,000. Sam's cutoff review finds: aluminum costing $15,000 shipped by a supplier FOB shipping point on December 29, arriving January 3; kayaks costing $22,000 at three dealers on consignment; paddles costing $9,000 held for a supplier on consignment; and kayaks costing $18,000 sold FOB shipping point on December 31, shipped that day, that were (correctly) not counted, but the sale was recorded on January 2.
What's wrong with the December 31 shipment, and its effect on income?

Inventory 760,000. The sale should be recorded in December: revenue and receivable understated by 28,800; COGS understated by 18,000 if perpetual not updated; income understated by 10,800. Dr AR 28,800 / Cr Sales 28,800; Dr COGS 18,000 / Cr Inventory 18,000 (if perpetual still shows it). Control: match shipping documents to invoices around year-end.
exam: Explain how goods in transit and consigned goods are treated, with examples.
FOB shipping point: buyer's when shipped; FOB destination: seller's until delivered; consigned goods stay with consignor until sold.
Explain the effect of an understated 2027 ending inventory of $22,000 on 2027 and 2028 financial statements.
2027: COGS over, NI under, RE under, current assets under. 2028: COGS under, NI over; RE correct by end of 2028.
